transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-16 14:00 PST
Duration: 41 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jenna Park, Marco Silva, Priya Nair (Redwood) - Liam O'Connor, Meera Patel, Sam Wu, Angela Ruiz (Helix Commerce)

[00:00] Jenna Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - I'm Jenna, AE on the account, with Marco our SE and Priya from devrel. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Liam O'Connor: Doing well, thanks. Excited to see the SDK stuff, we've skimmed the docs but want a guided runthrough.
[00:12] Marco Silva: Great, we'll walk through Python + TypeScript quickstarts, auth choices, env setup for hosted and Dedicated, and then outline a pilot. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:21] Meera Patel: Awesome, main thing for us is the auth + network setup - we need to make sure PII never leaves region and we use our KMS.
[00:28] Priya Nair: Totally understood, we'll cover KMS and VPC peering notes; also show how to toggle between hosted and a Dedicated instance via the SDK.
[00:35] Jenna Park: Quick context - Helix is planning to ship an in-product search + summarization feature Q1, target throughput about 50 qps with 1.5s p95 latency target. That's what Marco will help size.
[00:46] Marco Silva: Cool - i'll start share my screen - (screen share) - here's the repo, quickstart python. First step is install redwood-inference SDK, pip install redwood-inference (or npm i @redwood/inference for TS).
[01:02] (crosstalk)
[01:04] Marco Silva: Then you set your API key in an env var REDWOOD_API_KEY or configure SSO token if you use SAML. Example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx.
[01:15] Meera Patel: On SAML - we have SSO via Okta, we prefer short-lived tokens. Is there a service account flow?
[01:21] Marco Silva: Yes, we support SAML/OIDC for console access and short lived creds for programmatic access - we can mint temporary tokens via your IdP or use our service account with scoped keys. We'll send the exact steps in the security pack.
[01:33] Angela Ruiz: And for Dedicated, does auth change? We need KMS wrapped keys inside our VPC.
[01:39] Marco Silva: For Dedicated you can bring your KMS (customer-managed), we integrate via KMS endpoints and HSM if required. The SDK just points to the private endpoint - the auth flow is the same token model but tokens are issued by your control plane or our private control plane depending on the deployment.
[01:53] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Can you show a minimal Python generate call?
[01:57] Marco Silva: Sure - (typing) from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) ; resp = client.generate(model='redwood-13b', input='Summarize this order'). It's pretty much that. For streaming, you set stream=True and iterate.
[02:16] Meera Patel: Are there official examples for batching and async usage? We plan to batch request in workers.
[02:22] Marco Silva: Yes, we have an async client and batch helpers - see examples/async_batch.py. We also recommend using our built-in batching in Redwood Optimize which will suggest batching sizes per workload.
[02:34] Priya Nair: On the TS side - npm i @redwood/inference then: import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const out = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-13b', prompt: '...' });
[02:50] Sam Wu: Quick networking question - for Dedicated do we need to open a bunch of ports or just HTTPS outbound?
[02:55] Marco Silva: Mostly HTTPS outbound to the private endpoint if using private link or peering; if you use VPC peering there's some setup on your side but minimum ports - we'll share the exact firewall rules.
[03:07] Jenna Park: I'll pause here - any immediate red flags?
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: Two things: 1) data residency - we need RU/EU data residency for some customers; 2) logs and audit - we need long term audit logs hooked to our SIEM.
[03:20] Marco Silva: For data residency we have region pinning for hosted, and Dedicated gives you full residency control. Audit logs can be exported to your cloud (S3/Blob) or pushed to SIEM via our log forwarder. We also support syslog in private deployments.
[03:35] Meera Patel: About cost - we liked your Optimize suggestions but how deterministic is the savings? Our CFO wants ballpark numbers.
[03:42] Jenna Park: We can provide sample runbooks and a cost model. Typically batching + prefix caching can reduce per-token costs by 20-40% depending on workload; we'll run a pilot with your traffic to show concrete numbers.
[03:55] Marco Silva: Also note quantization options - some models run as int8 which reduces cost; tradeoff to check in evaluations.
[04:04] Angela Ruiz: For the pilot, what do you need from us?
[04:07] Marco Silva: Ideally: sample prompts, typical concurrency, training-free sample traffic or logs, and a clear success metric (p95 latency < x ms, quality delta < y on eval set).
[04:17] Meera Patel: We'll get sample traffic and a small eval set.
[04:20] (small pause)
[04:22] Marco Silva: Now quick demo of the SDK flow - I open python quickstart: step 1: set REDWOOD_API_KEY, step 2: choose model, step 3: call client.generate. For TypeScript similar. I'll show streaming example - sometimes the transcript will show partial tokens on the console.
[04:40] (typing noise)
[05:02] Marco Silva: One thing to watch: kv cache / prefix caching - if you have many repeated prefixes, Enable prefix cache in config and specify durable cache size. That reduces repeated compute. We call it the KV cache but some docs autocorrect to K-V cash - sorry for the grammar.
[05:20] Meera Patel: Is that cache in-memory on the GPU or external?
[05:24] Marco Silva: It can be in-process for small caches, or we can persist to a Redis cluster for shared caches across workers. For Dedicated we usually co-locate a small cache on the serving nodes plus a backing store.
[05:38] Liam O'Connor: Any gotchas with long context windows? We have 8k token docs.
[05:43] Marco Silva: Our runtime supports up to 32k in certain model variants; bigger context increases memory and latency - Optimize will recommend sequence-length aware kernels. We'll include benchmark numbers.
[05:56] Jenna Park: Quick note about security pack - we'll attach SOC2 report, pen-test summary, SAML config guide, and KMS integration doc.
[06:04] Angela Ruiz: Perfect. Also, do you provide SDK code samples for retries and idempotency? We need guaranteed exactly-once for certain workflows.
[06:12] Marco Silva: We have idempotency keys and recommended retry logic in the SDK. For critical flows use idempotency keys so duplicate generation calls are deduped on the server.
[06:21] Meera Patel: Can we see an example of the TS retry snippet?
[06:24] Priya Nair: (switches to TS example) Here we have a small wrapper that sets a unique requestId header and retries on 5xx with exponential backoff; stored in examples/retry.ts.
[06:36] Liam O'Connor: What's the SLA for Dedicated vs hosted?
[06:40] Jenna Park: Hosted has tiered SLAs; Dedicated gets an SLA with committed throughput and lower tail latencies - we'll include the SLA sheet.
[06:48] Sam Wu: We might prefer Dedicated for isolation. How long to provision?
[06:52] Marco Silva: Typical Dedicated lead time is 2-6 weeks depending on region and capacity; smaller pilots can run on hosted with VPC peering to emulate network conditions.
[07:02] Angela Ruiz: Onboarding: how long for our engineers to get basic integration running?
[07:05] Marco Silva: With the quickstart, a developer can run the hello-world example in under 30 minutes. Full integration with batching, retries, and the pilot benchmark would take 1-2 engineer-weeks.
[07:16] Meera Patel: Ok. For the pilot, can you host a small private instance or will we run sample traffic against hosted models?
[07:23] Marco Silva: We recommend starting hosted with region pinning and a private API key - that's fastest. If results show need for isolation we spin up Dedicated after. We'll size the Dedicated cluster after pilot.
[07:33] Jenna Park: Let's talk timeline - Helix aiming to ship Q1. If pilot in Jan and roll to prod in Feb we can align.
[07:42] Liam O'Connor: That works. Can you also confirm data retention options? We can't retain raw logs beyond 30 days for compliance.
[07:49] Marco Silva: We can configure retention in the Console and purge logs or forward them to your secure storage. Also, customer-managed keys ensure model inputs are encrypted at rest.
[07:59] Meera Patel: Any sample notebooks for local testing?
[08:02] Priya Nair: Yes - examples/notebooks contains python/ts notebooks that call the SDK and show streaming, batching, and eval harness integration. We'll send the quickstart repo link in the follow-up.
[08:14] (brief pause)
[08:18] Marco Silva: Before we wrap, quick walkthrough of the Console - (screen) Dashboard shows token usage, per-route latency, and Optimize suggestions. You can pin a model version and create a canary rollout.
[08:31] Angela Ruiz: Nice. Can we export metrics to Datadog?
[08:34] Marco Silva: Yes, we have exporters and webhooks to push traces and metrics.
[08:38] Meera Patel: On cost modeling - can you provide sample numbers for redwood-13b int8 vs 16-bit?
[08:44] Jenna Park: We'll include an approximate cost table in the follow-up; real numbers come from the pilot since token mix and prefix reuse matter a lot.
[08:53] Liam O'Connor: Any final questions from our side?
[08:55] Sam Wu: None here.
[08:56] Angela Ruiz: No.
[08:57] Meera Patel: One small ask - include sample Terraform for VPC peering steps if possible.
[09:02] Marco Silva: Will do, we'll add a terraform sample in the security pack.
[09:07] Jenna Park: Great, recap of next steps: we'll send pricing + security pack, Marco will send pilot scripts, Helix to share traffic. Proposed dates: pilot week Jan 4-8.
[09:18] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:20] Jenna Park: Thanks all - we'll follow up in email with links.
[09:25] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription has some small name errors (e.g., K-V cache sometimes transcribed oddly), filler words present, and occasional punctuation issues.
